title: A small overlay shows transform values to type in, and replaces the 3D panel section
goal: While the person moves, resizes, rotates or tilts an object, a small toolbar-like overlay appears next to it with the transform values they can type into and a Reset button. It goes away when they do something else or change tools. The 3D section in the panel is removed: its values live in this overlay.
notes:
User's words (2026-10-12): "I don't really see the point of adding a 3d pane just to show the rotation values. I think when we move or change transitions, we can show a small toolbar like overlay which shows the transform values for typing things in. But doing some other operation or changing the tool makes the transform overlay disappear. On the overlay there should be a reset button to reset to defaults. Also similarly, for when I have a keyframe and click the opacity dot, I want the same overlay to appear to tweak the opacity. Also editing the graph of a particular item like scale is really hard. I can right click on the scale, say show graph, but then when the graph is there, how do I add points on it? I click on the line, doesn't add a point, i can select a point but then if I have 2 points, I can't select the line in between. I want to be able to easily create nice transitions by adding points, selecting the segments between them, right clicking and changing their easing, etc. I need the ia to be consistent across the properties. When I add a 'key' to a video, it adds all of the animatable properties below it. I really wish there was a more scalable solution to the ux here, because we really should only show the properties being animated. And, if we want to clear one of them, i should be able to select one of the rows and hit delete to remove the whole property from being animated. but there should be a way to add it back. like maybe the keyframe line should be selectable and right clicked to animate a variety of things. or I can click it, tweak something (like transform) and the options are automatically added to that keyframe."

Five tasks, in order: the design (mocks), then the transform overlay, the key value overlay, the graph editor, and only-animated-properties with auto-key. The shared curve list is EasingCurve (PhotonzCore/LayerMotion.swift) with Draw a Curve, and CurveRow from every-transition-can-be-picked-from-presets-and. Memory rules: one purpose per area (the IA contract in docs/design/mocks/shared/UX-PATTERNS.md decides placement), mocks are the floor, legible text, no em dashes in UI copy. This is step 2 of 5.
acceptance: Built to the approved mock from 'Design the transform overlay and a simpler way to animate, as mocks' (mocks are the floor)

Placement and dismissal follow the mock's rules: 12pt under the object's frame, above it (over the turn knob) while a bottom handle is in hand or with no room below, slid to stay 12pt inside the canvas, never over the tool bar, keeping the side chosen at drag start; Reset is a text button that resets size, turn, tilt and depth and leaves position; the field the drag changes is outlined; a field shows a key diamond (filled on a key, hollow when animating) once the property animates; Layer > Show Transform Values opens it without a drag

The overlay appears when a transform starts (drag on a handle, nudge with arrows, a transform command) on any layer and stays while that object stays picked and nothing else is done; it shows only the values that apply (X, Y, W, H, Rotation for 2D; Tilt X, Tilt Y, Depth when the layer is in 3D or the 3D handles were used), updates live during the drag, and each field takes typed numbers and arithmetic (+10, *2) with Tab between fields and Return to commit
Reset returns the shown transform values to their defaults (no rotation, no tilt, depth 0, original size and the like) in one undo step

It disappears on: picking another tool, starting another kind of operation (typing text, drawing, picking another object, opening a menu), Escape, or clicking empty canvas; it never takes key from the canvas unless the person clicks into a field
The 3D section (Space3DInspector) leaves the panel; camera settings stay where the design puts them; nothing that was only reachable there is lost (every value is in the overlay or a menu)
Never covers the handle being dragged (placement moves aside), legible over any picture, MEASURED appear/disappear within one frame
A walk rotates and tilts a layer, types values in the overlay, presses Reset, changes tool and checks the overlay is gone

Adversarial pass before building: the canvas already had a dark drag pill 12pt under a dragged layer (drag readout), which would sit where the bar sits; the bar now carries those numbers for moves, resizes and 3D handles and the pill stays for sweeps and path reshapes. The panel's typed angle wrote the raw transform and never keyed, so the bar's values go through foldingIntoKeys and read the layer posed at the playhead, the way a canvas drag does. The 3D section's Pivot depth had to go somewhere, so it is on the bar once the layer is turned. Photoshop's analogue is Free Transform's options bar (X, Y, W, H, angle, typed): the bar meets that at the object instead of the top of the window.
